newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Filinvest Land sees 25-30 pct profit growth.
newsitem.headline: Filinvest Land sees 25-30 pct profit growth.

text.p: Filinvest Land Inc expected 25 to 30 percent growth in net income this year from robust demand for housing, Joseph Yap, company executive vice-president, told reporters on Friday.
The company reported net income of 2.02 billion pesos in 1996.
Yap said 50 percent of its revenues will come from social housing projects which cater to low-income families.
The lower middle-income housing projects will contribute 10 percent, while the middle and high-end residential projects will contribute 20 percent of the revenues.
The sale of golf shares is expected to contribute five percent, and the sale of subdivision lots, 15 percent.
Filinvest is scheduled to launch its 677-hectare golf and luxury residential community in eastern Manila by the second semester of the year.
First vice president Fely Ramos said the company had earmarked 750 million pesos for land acquisition. It planned to buy 250 to 300 hectares of raw land this year.
The capital expenditure will be sourced from its hefty cash position.
Development costs are likely to reach 1.75 billion pesos, but Ramos said it can be easily covered by pre-selling of residential units.
